build_inputs.angles:
1. Open on the two numbers together: Ford sells the Mustang GT with 450 horsepower, and this leaves Shelby American with about 825, from a Whipple supercharger bolted to the same 5.0-litre Coyote V8. Shelby adds 375 horsepower to a car Ford had already finished. Lead with that gap.

2. The thing most people watching will not know, and it changes how you see the whole car: this is not a Ford. Shelby American buys a finished Mustang GT and converts it after it has already been built and titled, which is why the base car has to be a 2021 to 2023 GT. You are watching a conversion, not a model line, and that is the honest framing for everything else in the video.

3. The money beat, and it is the uncomfortable one. Shelby American's own starting price for this build was about 140,000 dollars. In the same year Ford would sell you a factory Shelby GT500 with 760 horsepower for around 80,000. So you are paying roughly sixty thousand more for about sixty-five more horsepower and a Shelby serial number. Make that comparison the head-to-head beat, because the GT500 is the obvious rival and the numbers are brutal.

4. The history beat, and it is genuinely great: the first Super Snake, in 1967, was a single car. Shelby built it for Goodyear as a high-speed tyre test mule and put in a 427 essentially the same as the engine in the GT40 that had just won Le Mans, making around 600 horsepower. A run of fifty was planned and killed because it cost too much. One car existed. That is what the badge on this car is referring to.

5. Cover the catch honestly. It is a limited run and the number is on the car's own plate, so read the build number off the listing rather than guessing. And be straight about what a post-title conversion means for a buyer: the Ford warranty and the Shelby work are two different things, the value tracks the Shelby registry rather than the Mustang market, and 825 supercharged horsepower through the rear wheels is a lot to ask of a car that started as a 450 horsepower GT.

6. Close on the question: does bolting a supercharger and a serial number to a Mustang GT make it a Shelby, when the original Super Snake was one car with a Le Mans engine - or is that exactly what Carroll Shelby always did?

script: Ford stopped at 450 horsepower, but Shelby American says a Whipple adds 375 to the Coyote. The Shelby Super Snake 60th Anniversary takes its name from the one-off Shelby built in 1967 to test Goodyear tires with a Le Mans-spec GT40 427. Shelby starts with an already titled Mustang GT and swaps in a steel heat-extractor hood shared with the Carroll Shelby Signature Edition. There’s a spoiler back there to help counter lift. Shelby tuned the Borla exhaust around valves that can close to quiet the car and open when you want it louder. In stock form, that 5.0-liter V8 made 410 pound-feet of torque, and Shelby fitted high-flow injectors to feed it under boost. The six-speed manual sends everything to the rear wheels through a one-piece driveshaft. At about $140,000 new, would you have paid for the Shelby conversion or kept the GT the way Ford built it?

listing_facts.title: 2022 Ford Mustang Shelby Super Snake 60th Anniversary

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2022 Ford Mustang Shelby Super Snake 60th Anniversary, finished in Iconic Silver Metallic and Azure Blue with a black interior. This coupe is equipped with the desirable 6-speed manual transmission, and its odometer displays about 700 miles. The attached Carfax history report lists no accidents or mileage inconsistencies in this Mustang's past. This Mustang has been modified with the Super Snake 60th Anniversary Package from Shelby. According to a Shelby window sticker shown in the gallery, this package notably includes the Shelby Supercharger Package, high-performance fuel-injectors, a Shelby-tuned Borla variable exhaust system, and the Shelby Performance Track Handling suspension system. A window sticker is provided in the gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes heated and cooled front seats, a 12-speaker B&O sound system, and adaptive cruise control. The sixth-generation Mustang debuted for the 2015 model year, marking a significant evolution of Ford’s iconic pony car with independent rear suspension and advanced technology. The GT variant continues the tradition of offering V8 power and performance, appealing to driving enthusiasts seeking both modern amenities and classic muscle. Production ended in 2023. Power comes from a 5.0-liter supercharged V8, rated at 450 horsepower and 410 lb-ft of torque in stock form. Shelby states that its modifications increase horsepower to 825, but a dyno sheet was not provided to confirm. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
